method.trainingCodeChange: Only coding-tools.mjs among seven originally captured core modules changed after training, replacing keyword screening with Acorn AST policy before primary evaluation. Current code and lock hashes frozen for all primary and supplemental calls.
method.configurationAmbiguity: Original ordinary-object wording allowed a plain-object interpretation; hidden test required custom-prototype records. Original primary unchanged, exclusion and clarified-prompt supplement explicitly posthoc.

tasks.prompt:
Repair the TTL/LRU cache in src/cache.mjs and src/expiry.mjs, and run harness2_test after your changes. Inspect the sources and existing tests first. Keep the public exports and API.
createCache({capacity, ttl, now}) accepts a positive integer capacity and finite nonnegative ttl; invalid values throw RangeError. now defaults to Date.now and is an injected millisecond clock. set(key,value) stores any JavaScript value (including false, 0, null, and undefined), resets that key's deadline to now()+ttl, and makes the key most recently used. get(key) returns its stored value or undefined on a miss; a hit makes the key most recently used. has(key) distinguishes a stored undefined from a miss, without changing recency. size() counts only live entries. All operations remove expired entries before doing their work; an entry expires when now() >= its deadline. Reading does not extend a deadline. ttl=0 expires immediately. Inserting beyond capacity evicts the least recently used live key. Updating a live key must not evict another key. Preserve the dependency-free ES module layout and limit edits to the listed source files.

Repair mapLimit(items, limit, mapper) in src/map-limit.mjs and src/run-item.mjs, then run harness2_test. Inspect the existing implementation and tests first; keep the exports. mapLimit returns a Promise for an array in input order. Every item must invoke mapper(value,index) exactly once. Each output is {status:'fulfilled',value} or {status:'rejected',reason}, matching Promise.allSettled; preserve rejection reason identity, including synchronous mapper throws. A failed item must not stop other items. At most limit mapper calls may be in flight, and pending work must start as soon as a slot becomes free, without waiting for slower siblings in a batch. Support ordinary values, promises, and thenables returned by mapper. Empty input returns []; validate limit as a positive integer even for empty input, rejecting with RangeError otherwise. Non-array items and non-function mapper reject with TypeError. Do not mutate items. Keep source modules dependency-free and edit only the listed source files.

Repair collectPages(fetchPage, options) in src/collect-pages.mjs and src/merge-records.mjs, and run harness2_test. Inspect sources and existing tests first. Keep the ES module API and edit only listed source files.
Options default to {initialCursor:null,maxPages:100}. Call await fetchPage(cursor) sequentially, starting at initialCursor (default null); each page is {items,nextCursor}. items is an array of non-null record objects with id a string or finite number; nextCursor is either a string (including the empty string) or null. Null means stop, while an empty-string cursor must be fetched. Return deduplicated records in order of each id's first appearance, replacing a repeated id's entire record with its latest record. Numeric and string ids are distinct. Never mutate a page, its items, or the record objects. Detect repeated cursors including a return to the initial cursor, and throw an Error containing 'cursor' before fetching a cursor a second time. maxPages must be a positive integer, or throw RangeError before fetching. Fetch at most maxPages pages; if the last allowed page still points to another page, throw an Error containing 'limit'. A terminating page exactly at the limit succeeds. Malformed pages or records throw TypeError. Propagate fetch errors without swallowing or replacing them. No packages, network calls, or filesystem I/O are needed.

Repair planBuild(nodes) in src/plan-build.mjs and src/validate-nodes.mjs, then run harness2_test. Inspect the existing implementation/tests first. Preserve exports, use no external packages, and edit only the listed source files.
nodes is an array of {id,dependsOn}, with a nonempty string id and an array of dependency ids. An omitted dependsOn means no dependencies. Return a flat array of ids forming a deterministic topological order. At every step select the currently ready node appearing earliest in the original input, including nodes newly unblocked by the previous selection. Dependencies refer to ids, so declaration order is irrelevant. Repeated dependency ids count only once. Never mutate nodes, its record objects, or dependency arrays. Reject malformed nodes/dependencies with TypeError; ids and dependency ids must be nonempty strings. Reject duplicate node ids or references to missing ids with an Error containing 'duplicate' or 'missing' respectively. Reject self-dependencies and longer cycles with an Error containing 'cycle'; never return a partial schedule for these failures. Empty input returns []. Validate the complete graph before computing its schedule, so missing dependencies are reported even if a separate component contains a cycle.

Repair normalizeRanges(ranges) in src/normalize-ranges.mjs and subtractRanges(base, removed) in src/subtract-ranges.mjs. Ranges are half-open numeric intervals [start,end). Each argument must be an array, each member an array of exactly two finite numbers with start <= end; malformed inputs throw TypeError, reversed endpoints throw RangeError. Validate every member even if another member is empty or the eventual result is empty. normalizeRanges returns sorted, nonoverlapping ranges, merging both overlaps and touching endpoints; empty ranges disappear. subtractRanges returns the normalized set difference of the union of base and union of removed. It must split ranges when necessary, ignore removals outside base, and handle unsorted, duplicated, nested, negative and fractional intervals. Both functions return fresh outer and inner arrays and never mutate or reuse any input interval. Empty arrays are valid. No precision tolerance is used: compare numbers exactly.
Inspect the source and supplied public tests first, repair only the two listed source files, and run harness2_test. Keep exports and dependency-free ES modules; do not change tests.

Repair splitFrames(text, delimiter) in src/split-frames.mjs and createFramer(options) in src/framer.mjs. splitFrames accepts a string text and a nonempty string delimiter, otherwise throws TypeError. It returns {frames,rest}, consuming delimiter occurrences left to right without overlap; each preceding payload becomes one string frame, including empty payloads, and rest is the original suffix after the last complete delimiter. createFramer({delimiter='\r\n', maxBuffer=1024}={}) returns {push,finish}. delimiter follows the same validation; maxBuffer must be a finite nonnegative integer or throw RangeError. push accepts a string chunk (otherwise TypeError without changing pending data), and returns all newly completed frames. finish returns the final nonempty trailing payload as one frame, or [] when empty, then closes the framer. After successful finish, push or repeated finish throws Error containing 'closed'. Any chunk boundaries, including inside a multi-character delimiter, must match left-to-right one-shot splitting. Empty chunks do not create frames and consecutive delimiters do create empty frames. maxBuffer is a maximum frame payload length in JavaScript UTF-16 code units. On push, check each completed frame and the pending payload length, excluding the longest suffix that is a proper prefix of delimiter because that suffix may become a delimiter. On finish that suffix is ordinary payload and counts fully. Exceeding the limit throws RangeError; recovery after a length error is outside scope. Completed frames may not bypass the limit by arriving in one chunk, while any number of valid frames may arrive in one chunk. Do not trim or otherwise transform payloads; use no stream or external package.
Inspect the source and supplied public tests first, repair only the two listed source files, and run harness2_test. Keep exports and dependency-free ES modules; do not change tests.

Repair cloneValue(value) in src/clone-value.mjs and mergeLayers(...layers) with exported DELETE symbol in src/merge-layers.mjs. Values are acyclic JSON-like values: null, booleans, strings, finite numbers, arrays of values, and ordinary objects with enumerable own string keys. Undefined is additionally permitted only as an object property or a whole layer and means 'ignore this property/layer'. mergeLayers starts from an empty object and applies layers left to right. Each layer must be an ordinary non-null non-array object or undefined; other layers throw TypeError. For each property: undefined leaves the previous value unchanged; DELETE removes that property; two ordinary objects merge recursively; otherwise the incoming value replaces the previous value. Arrays always replace, never concatenate or merge by index. DELETE may appear as a direct object property at any nesting level, including inside a newly introduced object; it may not appear inside an array. A deleted property can later be recreated. Null, false, 0 and empty strings are literal replacements. Inherited properties are ignored. Results use ordinary objects and arrays; return a deep copy so no result container aliases any input container or prior call's result. cloneValue follows the same accepted value model, ignores undefined/DELETE object properties, and rejects top-level undefined/DELETE, non-finite numbers, functions, symbols other than DELETE as object-property commands, nonordinary objects, and invalid array elements with TypeError. mergeLayers must validate all incoming content even when it would replace an existing value. Input containers may be frozen and must never be mutated. Circular structures and unusual property descriptors are outside scope.
Inspect the source and supplied public tests first, repair only the two listed source files, and run harness2_test. Keep exports and dependency-free ES modules; do not change tests.

Repair runWithRetry(operation, options) in src/retry.mjs and retryDelay(attempt, options) in src/retry-delay.mjs; inspect sources/tests and run harness2_test. Keep exports and dependency-free ES modules, edit only the listed source files.
runWithRetry is async and invokes operation(attempt), with attempt starting at 1. Defaults are maxAttempts=3, baseDelay=10, maxDelay=1000, shouldRetry=()=>true, sleep=async()=>{}. The default sleep is intentionally a no-op; callers inject a real wait. An ordinary value, promise, or thenable resolving to any value is success. Handle synchronous throws and rejected promises identically. On failure, if this was the last permitted attempt, throw that exact reason without invoking shouldRetry or sleep. Otherwise await shouldRetry(reason,attempt); its truthiness permits retry and falsey means rethrow the exact operation reason. If permitted, await sleep(retryDelay(attempt,{baseDelay,maxDelay}),attempt+1) fully before invoking the next attempt. Exceptions/rejections from shouldRetry or sleep propagate unchanged and stop retries. Never sleep or invoke shouldRetry after success. Never mutate options.
retryDelay takes the failed one-based attempt and returns min(maxDelay, baseDelay * 2**(attempt-1)); cap overflow to finite maxDelay, and a zero baseDelay always returns zero even for very large attempts. Defaults for its delay options are the same as above. Validate attempt and maxAttempts as positive integers; baseDelay and maxDelay as finite nonnegative numbers; invalid numbers throw RangeError. Validate operation, shouldRetry, and sleep as functions or throw TypeError. runWithRetry must validate all options before its first operation, even if that operation would succeed. The helper must also validate its own numeric inputs. No timers, clocks, packages, network, or filesystem are needed.

Repair parseCsv(text) and serializeCsv(rows) in src/csv.mjs and encodeCsvField(value) in src/csv-field.mjs. Inspect sources and tests, preserve exports, edit only the listed modules, and run harness2_test. Use dependency-free ES modules.
parseCsv returns an array of nonempty arrays of string fields. Commas delimit fields. Outside quotes CRLF, bare LF, and bare CR delimit records. An empty document returns []; a blank record returns ['']. A final record delimiter ends the last record without adding a phantom record, so '\n' has one blank record and '\n\n' has two. A trailing comma creates a final empty field. A quoted field starts with a double quote at the beginning of that field; within it doubled double quotes decode to one quote, and comma/CR/LF are literal data, preserving embedded newline bytes exactly. After the closing quote only a comma, record delimiter, or end of document is permitted. Reject unclosed quotes, quotes inside unquoted fields, or characters after a closing quote with SyntaxError. Do not trim whitespace, strip BOM, or normalize field contents. Non-string input throws TypeError.
serializeCsv accepts an array of nonempty row arrays containing strings only, and must not mutate it. Invalid rows/fields throw TypeError. Encode fields with encodeCsvField: quote any empty field or any field containing comma, double quote, CR, or LF; double every quote inside a quoted field; leave other strings byte-for-byte unchanged. The helper itself rejects non-string input with TypeError. Join fields with commas and records with CRLF, with no final record delimiter. serializeCsv([]) is ''. The quoted empty field makes [['']] distinguishable from an empty document. For any valid rows, parseCsv(serializeCsv(rows)) must equal rows. No packages, Node APIs, filesystem, or network are needed.

limitations: Training and holdout samples are dependent within each frozen harness round.
The cursor regression is now a known evaluation case; heldout means excluded from these training calls, not unknown to the experiment designer.
Unavailable arms count as unsuccessful in planned-pipeline rates; semantic analysis is separately restricted to eligible successful native calls.
Completed pairs means both scores were collected, including native/grading failures; semantic-eligible pairs exclude these failures and invalid hidden-test counts.
Native milliseconds sum provider sessions; concurrent elapsed time and human repair time are different quantities.
Planned incremental time excludes the ordinary training-task baseline; from-scratch time charges all training calls. Transport and native timings are reported separately.

Missing or zero-duration failed native sessions make native cost ratios and break-even estimates unavailable; observed native sums are lower bounds only. Host transport timing is independent and may remain complete.
Amortization at 24/100 tasks is a timing scenario holding the observed effect fixed, not evidence that the quality benefit generalizes beyond these tasks.
No token or monetary price is inferred; source-screening is conservative and not a general hostile-JavaScript trust boundary.
Three hand-authored-task rounds and one training task do not establish general coding quality or exact reproducibility of model samples.
All three training runs had failed intermediate stages even though each produced a valid aggregate.
Many NATIVE_TURN_FAILED calls occurred; their detailed cause is not established. They are not silently recast as reasoning failures.
The supplemental clarified prompt remains a posthoc sensitivity; failed native sessions cannot adjudicate its source contract.
A new cursor sentinel variant escaped the fixed primary cases, so primary success is not proof of complete functional correctness.
Observable retry replay is retrospective reuse of existing chronological round samples, not a new online cost-matched experiment or hidden-oracle selection.
Runtime versions and bridge hashes were observed during primary evaluation; no retroactive claim of native/SDK binary hashing at training start.
